Pushed as `6f105c6`.

## Report — housekeeping, 2026-09-29 21:45 ET

**Nothing was due.** `due.py t2-list` was empty, no event has an open snapshot session for this ET day, and this step gated nothing, froze nothing and wrote no decision. No T2 decisions to report. MU (frozen INELIGIBLE `thin_oi` at 14:31 ET by the first fire of the day) is still the only gate in the pilot's history.

**Freezes today:** one, from the earlier run — `6da4a56` MU 2026-09-30, **BLIND** (committed 14:31:08 ET, entry open 2026-09-30 09:30 ET). Nothing new from this run.

**PENDING changes: none.** AEHR is the last PENDING name and stays PENDING — and it is now two days late against its own pattern. The newsroom's newest item is still the Sep 28 CEO Investor Summit release, which is a conference, not an earnings date; EDGAR's newest filings are annual-meeting material with no 8-K carrying a date; yfinance still says Nov 2 intraday and Nasdaq still says Oct 5 with no time. Its earliest possible snapshot session is Thu Oct 1, so **one housekeeping run remains** (Wed Sep 30) before code marks it INELIGIBLE `unconfirmed`. Expect that. Code's `find_dates` ran first and recorded `no_feed` — AEHR has no machine-readable IR feed, so this name will always need the AI leg.

**Two things went wrong, both infrastructure, both needing a laptop session:**

1. **`check.py` now FAILS inside this checkout** — it reports `T1_rule_v0.json` and `D006_history_study_v1.md` as "missing frozen registry files". They are missing on purpose: the sparse-checkout fence removes them so T2 cannot see the T1 rule. `check.py` can't tell "fenced out" from "deleted", so every T2 and housekeeping run from here on will read FAIL. The record is intact — `git ls-files` shows all three files still tracked, and code ran the real health check in the full checkout before this step. It needs a fence-aware skip, or the AI step should stop running it, because a health check that cries wolf every run is worse than none.
2. **`actions: read` didn't take effect.** `gh run list` still returns HTTP 403 even though `c2853d6` added the grant three hours before this run — the token was minted from the workflow definition in force at run start. It should work on the next run; until it does, the 09-28-style question "did the fire arrive, or did the code crash silently" still can't be answered from inside the runner.

**Tomorrow:** NKE, snapshot Wed Sep 30, AMC Oct 1 — the first event that can reach a T2 decision, and the first live test of the per-event `t2` job.
